author: Andrew Donovan
title: DA expects charges against people 'other than just the driver' in DWI crash that killed three-year-old - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Donovan ,
5 hours ago
SYRACUSE, N.Y. (WSYR-TV) — The Onondaga County District Attorney expects charges against people other than the driver involved in the drunk driving crash that killed a three-year-old in Syracuse.
Who is facing the charges remains unknown.
Three-year-old Yasmeen Shaaf was the backseat passenger in an SUV, along with her mother and brother, that police said was driven drunk by the girlfriend of the girl’s mother.
The driver, 25-year-old Jazmine Vann, is accused of driving drunk, going at least 70 miles per hour through the city’s north side before the vehicle hit a curb, flew through the air more than 30 feet, and smashed into a tree.
Among Vann’s 17 charges, she was ticketed for not properly restraining the children within the vehicle. For the first time, DA Bill Fitzpatrick confirmed a car seat found by police at the scene wasn’t used before the crash.
“No restraint on the three-year-old,” explained Fitzpatrick. “No car seat. No seatbelt. Nothing.”
Between the drunk driving and lack of restraint, the multiple levels of danger the children were in have members of the community questioning the decisions of the other adult in the SUV — the children’s mother.
When asked about the girl’s mother being charged, the DA wouldn’t specify. “I’m not trying to be coy, but there will be more charges against people… other than just the driver,” he said.
The case will be heard by an Onondaga County Grand Jury, which will vote for or against any charges against anyone involved.
